items.prompt: A zero-coupon bond has positive face and a target within the declared yield bracket. Why can its inverse yield still be unique?

options.text: Its positive terminal redemption makes price strictly decreasing in yield.
options.why: Positive earlier coupons are not required: in this zero-coupon case the positive terminal redemption alone gives strict monotonicity.

options.text: Zero coupon means the whole bond has zero value.
options.why: The positive face is still repaid at maturity.

options.text: The routine invents an extra positive coupon.
Every possible yield produces the same discount factor.
options.why: A positive future redemption changes present value as yield changes.
